devices.name: Hard drive (internal HDD)
devices.blurb: Spinning magnetic disk inside a desktop or laptop. Often recoverable if you act early.

devices.name: SSD (SATA and NVMe)
devices.blurb: Flash-based internal drive. Deleted data can be hard to get back because of TRIM.

devices.name: USB flash drive
devices.blurb: Small thumb drive plugged into a USB port. Simple to image and often easy to rescue.

devices.name: SD / microSD card
devices.blurb: Memory card from cameras, phones and drones. Usually recoverable with the right tools.

devices.name: External / portable drive
devices.blurb: Hard drive or SSD in a USB enclosure. Check the enclosure and the drive separately.

symptoms.name: Deleted files
symptoms.blurb: Files were removed or emptied from the trash. The data may still be on the drive.

symptoms.name: Accidentally formatted
symptoms.blurb: You formatted the drive by mistake. A quick format usually leaves files in place.

symptoms.name: Not detected / not showing up
symptoms.blurb: Your computer does not see the drive at all. The cause may be cable, port or power.

symptoms.name: Clicking or grinding noises
symptoms.blurb: A repeated click or grind from a spinning drive. Power it off soon to limit damage.

symptoms.name: Won't power on / dead
symptoms.blurb: The drive shows no lights, no spin or no response when connected.

symptoms.name: Water, fire or physical damage
symptoms.blurb: The drive was wet, burned, dropped or crushed. Do not power it on again.

symptoms.name: Corrupted / RAW / asks to format
symptoms.blurb: Windows or macOS says the drive needs formatting or shows as RAW.

symptoms.name: Encrypted or locked
symptoms.blurb: The drive asks for a password or key, such as BitLocker, FileVault or VeraCrypt.

testdisk.name: TestDisk
testdisk.desc: Free open-source tool that finds lost partitions and repairs boot sectors so files can be read again.

photorec.name: PhotoRec
photorec.desc: Free open-source file carver that recovers files by signature, even when the file system is damaged.

ddrescue.name: GNU ddrescue
ddrescue.desc: Copies a failing drive to an image file, retrying bad areas so you work from a copy, not the original.

ddrescueview.name: ddrescueview
ddrescueview.desc: Free graphical viewer that shows which parts of a ddrescue image are good, bad or still unread.

hddsuperclone.name: HDDSuperClone
hddsuperclone.desc: Linux tool for cloning a failing drive sector by sector, with options that skip and retry bad areas.

smartmontools.name: smartmontools
smartmontools.desc: Free open-source suite that reads S.M.A.R.T. health data from drives to show early signs of failure.

crystaldiskinfo.name: CrystalDiskInfo
crystaldiskinfo.desc: Free Windows app that shows a drive's S.M.A.R.T. health status, temperature and other key attributes.

f3.name: F3 (Fight Flash Fraud)
f3.desc: Free open-source tool that tests flash drives and cards for fake capacity, so you know what they really hold.

h2testw.name: H2testw
h2testw.desc: Free Windows tool that writes and verifies test files to check that a flash drive stores data correctly.

ncfi.name: National Computer Forensics Institute (NCFI)
ncfi.desc: US Secret Service training center for law enforcement. A reference only; not a consumer recovery service.

fbi-rcfl.name: FBI Regional Computer Forensics Laboratory (RCFL)
fbi-rcfl.desc: FBI-run labs that serve law enforcement cases. A reference only; not a consumer recovery service.

brett-shavers.name: Brett Shavers
brett-shavers.desc: Personal site of a digital forensics and incident response author and expert, with articles and books.

dfir-training.name: DFIR.training
dfir-training.desc: Digital forensics and incident response training and resources, run by Brett Shavers.

nist-cftt.name: NIST Computer Forensics Tool Testing (CFTT)
nist-cftt.desc: NIST program that tests forensic tools against defined requirements and publishes the results.

sleuthkit-autopsy.name: The Sleuth Kit / Autopsy
sleuthkit-autopsy.desc: Open-source digital forensics toolkit and its Autopsy graphical interface, used to analyze disk images.

hddguru-forum.name: HDD Guru Forums
hddguru-forum.desc: Community forum for hard drive hardware, firmware, data recovery and HDD-related questions.

cgsecurity-forum.name: CGSecurity Forum
cgsecurity-forum.desc: Official community forum for TestDisk and PhotoRec, where users ask questions and share results.
